fields.launchWriteup: Launch week was 1-7 September. On 1 Sep at about 11pm I moved Razorpay out of test mode and put the ₹1,200/month plan live on the site, no free trial. On 2 and 3 Sep I stood outside the gym on Karve Road from 7:15am with a printed UPI QR and a dabba in my hand and talked to whoever came out - 34 conversations across the two mornings, 9 people scanned, 2 subscribed the same day. On 4 Sep I posted a 40 second video of the morning packing run in the two Kothrud PG groups I am actually a member of (188 and 96 members), and on 5 Sep the third subscription came from that post. On 6 Sep I boosted an Instagram reel for ₹500 targeted to Kothrud and Karvenagar: 4,100 views, 0 signups, and I would not spend that ₹500 again. Two things did not work. The boost, obviously. And the 'first week free' I ran in August - 3 people took the free week and none of them paid after, so I killed it before launch and charged from day one instead. Numbers: 3 paying subscribers, ₹3,600 collected, which the tracker reads as $43.37 gross and $42.35 net after Razorpay's cut. For the next hundred I would stop treating the gym as a channel and start asking every subscriber for the flat number of one neighbour who eats out daily, because both my gym signups came with a neighbour's name attached and I did nothing with them.
fields.distributionChannels:
Gym gate, Karve Road, 2 and 3 Sep mornings: 34 conversations, 9 QR scans, 2 paid subscriptions. Best channel by far and also the slowest - two hours standing per morning.
PG WhatsApp groups (2 groups, 188 and 96 members): 1 video post each on 4 Sep, 41 video views that I can see, 6 people messaged me, 1 subscribed on 5 Sep. The rest asked about Jain food which I do not do yet.
Instagram reel, boosted ₹500 on 6 Sep: 4,100 views, 38 profile visits, 0 signups. Nothing. I think the audience was right and the reel was bad - it was 40 seconds of rice.
r/pune, 1 post on 3 Sep asking what people hate about their current dabba: 27 comments, 0 signups, but 4 of those comments are why I moved the delivery slot from 1pm to 12:30pm.
My own college society list: I did not use it. Everyone there is on hostel mess food and would have signed up to be nice, which is not a customer.
Society noticeboard in my building: 1 A4 poster on 5 Sep, 0 calls, ₹0 spent, still up.
fields.firstCustomerStory: My first customer is the man who runs the xerox and lamination shop under my building. He is about 50, eats from a plastic box his wife packs at 6am, and by 1pm it is cold because there is no microwave in the shop. I have been printing assignments there for two years so this was not a cold approach and I want to be honest about that - but he found the product from the A4 poster I stuck on the shop shutter on 1 Sep, not from me asking him. On 2 Sep morning he called me up and the first thing he said was 'roti garam rahegi kya 1 baje tak?' - he did not ask the price first, he asked about the roti. I said the box holds heat for about two hours and he could try one day before subscribing, and he said no, he'll just take the month. He paid ₹1,200 on the Razorpay link at 9:41am on 2 Sep, UPI, first payment on the account. After that he has eaten 11 of 12 delivered dabbas, skipped one Thursday because the shop was shut, and on 9 Sep he asked me on WhatsApp whether I can do a second box for his helper at a lower price. That request is the reason I am now working out a two-box rate. He also complains about the sabzi being too oily every second day, which I am told is a good sign.

notes: Dated day-by-day actions, every channel carries a number or an honest 'nothing', the first customer is a traceable person with an arrival path and a post-payment behaviour, the learning names a specific change plus two things that failed, and ₹3,600 across 3 subscribers matches the tracker's $43.37 and 3 paying customers. All six criteria met.
